reason: This could mean two different things. 'With a terminal leaf' reads like a pinnate leaf ending in a leaflet, which would be terminal leaflet (FLOPO_0996015). 'Conduplicada/involuta' reads like the uppermost leaf blade of a grass culm, which is an upper leaf (FLOPO_0996003) or a leaf lamina. The examples do not show which is meant, and the two need different targets.

label: crownshaft
parent: is_a PO_0025269 collective organ part structure; part_of PO_0009006 shoot system
definition: A collective organ part structure (PO:0025269) composed of the tubular leaf sheaths (PO:0020104) of the uppermost leaves of a palm, which tightly enclose one another to form a smooth, often coloured column at the top of the stem (PO:0009047), below the leaf crown.
reason: This is the same structure as 'crownshaft', which was decided new_class on 2026-11-14 and is not yet in the ID registry. 'crown shaft' should become a synonym of that proposed class, not a separate term. The qualities (shining, greenish, swollen, elongated) belong to the shaft as a whole, not to one leaf sheath. It should be proposed upstream to PO.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656), the cyathial gland; pattern 12, part of a stated whole
reason: These are the horn-like extensions of the Euphorbia cyathial gland ('tips extended into 2 slender horns'). This follows the earlier 'gland appendage' decision, which targeted PO_0005656 with the part-of pattern. The horns are the drawn-out tips of the gland, so they map to its apex region. A count of horns is a count of that region on the gland.

target: leaf sheath (PO_0020104), apex region via slot 1, as decided for 'leaf sheath mouth'; concave or straight is the outline of that apex edge
reason: This is the edge of the sheath mouth. 'Leaf sheath mouth' was mapped on 2026-11-23 to the apex region of the leaf sheath. 'Concave' and 'straight' describe the outline of that edge, so no extra class is needed.

This is a misspelling of areola, which can mean many things. At 12-27 µm across it is far too small for a cactus areole (PO_0025353) or a leaf lamina areole (PO_0025392). It is more likely a sculpture unit of a pollen, spore or seed-coat surface. The examples do not name the organ.

label: cell papilla
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of FLOPO_0986100 laminal cell
definition: A small solid outgrowth of the outer wall of a plant cell (PO:0009002), especially of a laminal cell of a bryophyte leaf, which may be simple or branched. Unlike a leaf papilla cell (PO:0025167), it is a part of one cell, not a cell itself.
reason: This is the same as the 'cell papilla' proposed on 2026-11-23 (from 'papillae per cell'), which is not yet in the ID registry. It should not be a second class. The statements say it is simple or branched, large, and 1 (or 2) per cell. These describe the papilla itself, so stating them as qualities of the laminal cell would be wrong. It should be proposed upstream to PO together with the earlier item.
Exact: a misspelling of propagule ('Vegetative popagules small, deciduous'). 'Asexual propagulum' was mapped to the same class on 2026-11-23.

A height of 45-100 µm suggests the basal membrane of a moss peristome. However, the examples do not say whether it belongs to the exostome, the endostome (FLOPO_0986125 endostome basal membrane) or a single peristome. Picking one would be a guess.
Exact: these are the leaves of the moss perigonium. 'Perigonial leaf' was mapped to PO_0030028 on 2026-11-14.

The examples only say it is absent or present and never name the organ that bears it. 'Abaxial' together with 'terminal' does not fit the plain apex mapping used for 'terminal spine' (FLOPO_0985023). 'Apical spine' was also rejected on 2026-11-23.
The organ is not named. It could be a tooth of a leaf lamina, calyx, lemma or bract, and each needs a different container. 'Lateral tooth' was rejected for the same reason on 2026-11-23.

target: stem cortex (PO_0025612) part of branch (PO_0025073), container rule
reason: This is the Sphagnum branch cortex ('enlarged, with conspicuous retort cells'): the cortex of the branch stem, as opposed to the main stem. The retort cells inside it are the separate class proposed on 2026-11-14.

target: prickle (PO_0025169) with position below the stipule (PO_0020041), pattern 09 relation to another part; counted per node
reason: Narrower: a prickle placed below the stipules. 'Infrastipular' was sent to pattern 09 (relation to another part) on 2026-11-14.

target: hyaline cell (FLOPO_0986077) part of costa (PO_0030072), container rule; the number of layers, abaxial or adaxial, is the quality
reason: Leucocysts are the hyaline cells of Leucobryum-type costae. The statements count the layers these cells form on each side of the costa. A layer is not a separate structure, so no class is needed.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of phyllome lamina tooth (PO_0025515), count with container
reason: This counts the cells that make up a marginal tooth ('teeth of 1 cell', '3-4 cells each'). It follows the 2026-11-23 decision for 'leaf lobe cell', which used the same container rule.

target: native plant cell (PO_0025606) part of vaginant lamina (FLOPO_0986095), container rule
reason: In moss floras the 'sheath lamina' is the vaginant lamina of Fissidens-type leaves. 'Vagrant lamina cell' was given the same target on 2026-11-23. The cell surface qualities (smooth, papillate, verrucose) are stated of these cells.

Exact: 'marginal flower' is already listed as a synonym of the positioned part outer flower (FLOPO_0996039), and 'marginal floret' as a narrower one. 'Flores marginales 0-4' counts these flowers in a head.
Narrower: ☿ marks bisexual flowers. 'Hermaphrodite flower' and 'perfect flower' are synonyms of PO_0009046. The count goes to flower, with the bisexual condition as a quality if needed.
Exact: ♀ marks female flowers, and 'female flower' is a synonym of PO_0025599.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part of trunk (FLOPO_0985025), pattern 12; stem base (PO_0008039) is the PO equivalent
reason: This is the base of a tree trunk ('à base cannelée, lobée, munie de contreforts'). Both the trunk and the base region exist as classes. 'Buttressed' can also be stated as the presence of buttress root (FLOPO_0986085).

These are 'cloisons' 0.5-4 mm high, but the examples do not show what they divide or in which family they occur. They could be internal ridges of the hypanthium, septa between stamen groups, or walls in a receptacle. None of septum (PO_0000030), plant ovary septum (PO_0025262) or fruit septum (PO_0025268) fits for certain.

target: outer tepal (FLOPO_0996032) part of staminate flower (PO_0025600), container rule
reason: 'External tepal' was mapped to outer tepal (FLOPO_0996032) on 2026-11-23. Here it is qualified by the male flower, which is its container.

target: inner tepal (FLOPO_0996037) part of staminate flower (PO_0025600), container rule
reason: 'Internal' tepal ('les internes plus petits') is the inner tepal of a positioned series. It is qualified by the male flower, which is its container.
Narrower: the claw is the narrowed basal part of a bract. Earlier, 'tepal claw' was mapped to tepal base and 'corolla claw' to petal base.
Exact: French for bracteole. 'Alternes' is a quality that was split off as a fragment and should be read as alternate.

Narrower: 'crypte' and 'domacios del tipo cripta' name a crypt-type (pit) domatium. The crypt type is a kind of domatium and is better stated as a quality than as a class. Depth and 'deep' then apply to the domatium.
Exact: a misspelling of 'gynoecium rudiment', which was mapped to pistillode on 2026-11-23.

target: perianth lobe (FLOPO_0986004) part of staminate flower (PO_0025600), container rule
reason: This counts and measures the perianth lobes of the male flower ('4-5 lobes, 1.5-3 mm long'). Perianth lobe is the general class. If the source says calyx or corolla, calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005) or corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) can be used instead.
This is the stipe of a legume pod. It follows the 2026-11-23 decisions for 'fruit stipe' and 'achene stipe': a stalk inside a fruit container. 'Pod' is a synonym of legume fruit.

Probably exact. In French flora descriptions 'ramifications primaires', few in number and 6-10 cm long, are usually the primary branches of a panicle. 'Primary inflorescence branch' is a synonym of PO_0006321. If the source describes the shoot rather than the inflorescence, this should be first-order branch (PO_0025073) instead.
